title: Music Hackspace
desc: Creative coding, music technology and community since 2011 — courses, hackathons and tutorials in Max/MSP, TouchDesigner, Ableton and more, run out of London.

title: Acid Solder Club
desc: DIY electronics and synth-building workspace in Utrecht, NL — bring-your-own-electronics soldering sessions, hackathons and skill-shares for all levels.

title: London Hackspace
desc: The East London makerspace Hackoustic calls home — open access to tools, electronics and a community of hackers of every kind.

title: CLIP Sound and Music
desc: Colchester-based social enterprise, founded by sound artist Frazer Merrick and Simon Keep, running accessible music-tech workshops for young people across Essex and East Anglia. Hackoustic has worked with them before.

title: UK Hackspace Foundation
desc: A directory and map of hackspaces and makerspaces across the UK — a good starting point for finding (or starting) a space outside London.

title: South London Makerspace
desc: Member-run community workshop in Herne Hill with electronics benches, laser cutting, textiles, wood and metal shops, and a weekly electronics meet-up.

title: Bela
desc: Open-source embedded platform for ultra-low-latency interactive audio, built by the Augmented Instruments Laboratory at Queen Mary University of London — a favourite for building responsive digital instruments.

title: Spoke
desc: Turns any conductive object or material into a touch-based MIDI, keyboard or serial controller — a fast way to build instruments, soundboards and interactive installations with no extra software.

title: Look Mum No Computer
desc: Sam Battle's site and YouTube channel documenting the build of wild analogue synths and instruments — Furby organs, synth bikes and more, most with full build videos.

title: dadamachines
desc: Berlin-based studio making modular hardware kits, like the Automat toolkit, that turn everyday objects into playable instruments.

title: Drake Music
desc: UK charity working where music, disability and technology meet — accessible instrument design, DMLab seed-funding grants, and a growing national collection of accessible instruments.

title: Pure Data (Pd)
desc: Free, open-source visual programming language for audio, video and sensor processing — a common building block for custom instruments and installations.

title: SuperCollider
desc: Open-source platform for audio synthesis and algorithmic composition, widely used in live coding and generative sound art.

title: Adafruit Learning System
desc: A huge library of free, step-by-step electronics tutorials — from a first solder joint to complex sensor and microcontroller projects.

title: SparkFun Learn
desc: Clear guides on electronics fundamentals, plus a well-stocked parts catalogue for anyone building their own hardware.

title: Instructables
desc: Community-submitted, step-by-step project guides spanning electronics, music and craft — good for searching a specific build technique.

title: Freesound
desc: A huge library of user-submitted sound recordings under Creative Commons licences — useful for sampling and sound design.

title: Notes and Volts
desc: Dave's long-running blog and YouTube channel of DIY synth and Arduino-based MIDI projects, with full build guides, code and schematics for each one.

title: Moritz Klein
desc: In-depth, beginner-friendly YouTube series building analogue synth circuits from scratch — VCOs, filters, wavefolders and more, explained intuitively with minimal maths.

title: Sound on Sound
desc: Long-running UK magazine covering music technology, recording and sound design in depth.

title: CDM (Create Digital Music)
desc: News, tutorials and community coverage of music technology, software and hardware, with a strong focus on experimental and DIY practice.

title: Handmade Electronic Music
desc: Nicolas Collins's widely-recommended book on circuit bending and hardware hacking — a hands-on introduction to building noise-making circuits with little to no electronics background needed.
